title: Magnetite promotes volatile solids degradation under wet pit latrine conditions
content: Conductive mineral additives have been proposed to enhance anaerobic digestion, but their value for reducing pit latrine filling remains poorly characterised. This study evaluated magnetite addition during anaerobic digestion of synthetic human excreta under simulated wet pit latrine conditions. Magnetite was added at 0–8 g L−1 across three independent batch assays under mesophilic conditions. Volatile solids reduction increased significantly at 4 and 8 g L−1 reaching approximately 11% above the control, while cumulative methane yield and methanogenic functional markers remained unaffected by treatment. Residual volatile fatty acid accumulation and extracellular polymeric substance carbohydrate concentrations increased with magnetite dose, indicating that the primary effect was enhanced upstream particulate conversion without stimulation of terminal methanogenesis. Microbial and predicted functional responses were concentrated in hydrolytic, fermentative and iron-associated markers, whereas syntrophic, methanogenic and DIET-related responses remained stable or batch-dependent. Mass-balance threshold analysis showed that a net reduction in pit filling requires total solids contents substantially exceeding those typical of wet pit latrine. These findings indicate that magnetite has potential as a low-dosage mineral amendment for pit latrine management, but field validation under realistic operational conditions is required.
